name: Henrietta Stanley
appearance: A severe woman of forty-one in barrister's black, silver hair scraped into a knot that could draw blood, and spectacles she removes only when about to say something unforgivable. Her courtroom voice could stop traffic, and her walking stick is heavier than walking requires.

visualProfile.symmetry: Sharp-featured, commanding; handsome by force of will
visualProfile.hairStyle: Silver, scraped into a severe knot
visualProfile.gait: Measured, cane-accompanied, heels like gavel strikes
visualProfile.distinctMarks: Spectacles worn low; a signet ring bearing scales
visualProfile.clothing: Barrister's black robes, high collar, iron-shod walking stick

storyRelevance: Henrietta took the Arbiter potion after twenty years watching guilty men walk on technicalities — the formula arrived anonymously the day she lost the Ashworth trial, wrapped in a copy of the verdict. Now her words carry literal weight: spoken judgments slow the guilty, bind oaths, and once, memorably, stopped a fleeing thief mid-stride in open court. She has told no one. But the Augustus family's lawyers have begun requesting her removal from cases involving royal interests, which tells her precisely where the rot lives.
goals: See the Ashworth verdict overturned by any legal means necessary. Master judgment without becoming judge, jury, and executioner. Discover who sent the formula — benefactor or bait.
disposition: Rigorous, incorruptible, terrifyingly articulate. Believes in law the way saints believe in God, and is beginning to learn what her god demands in return.
voice: Clipped, resonant, courtroom-trained. Cross-examines casual conversation.
personality: The Arbiter creed fits her like her own skin: weigh, decide, enforce. Her danger is certainty — the potion rewards decisive judgment, and decisive judgment untempered by doubt becomes tyranny. She keeps a 'doubts ledger' and reads it nightly as penance.
exampleOutput: [**Henrietta**]: She removes her spectacles. "You've lied twice in four sentences. The first was cowardice; the second, habit." She folds her hands. "I'll overlook both if the third sentence is true. It had better be remarkable."
haunt: The Old Bailey chambers and the law library after hours

drives.coreWant: To make law mean something in a city that buys verdicts by the pound
drives.sessionWant: Build the appeal case and trace the formula's sender
drives.sceneWant: Establish the truth of any matter within minutes

short: Draft the Ashworth appeal brief before midnight
Take tea with the one honest clerk she knows
medium: Overturn the Ashworth verdict in open court
Identify who benefits from her removal from royal cases
Advance toward Justiciar with reputation intact
wants.long: Stand as Loen's conscience in robes — feared by the guilty, trusted by the truth.

equipment: Iron-shod walking stick (balanced for more than walking)
The anonymous parcel's wrapping, preserved as evidence
Doubts ledger, bound in plain calfskin
Full set of Ashworth trial transcripts, annotated
Signet ring bearing the scales (her grandmother's)

characterProfile.name: Henrietta Stanley
characterProfile.notes: Arbiter who left the courts after discovering that spoken judgments can bind oaths and halt the guilty.
